architectureDecisions: CrossDomainObligation is an immutable WHAT contract from one accepted semantic publication to another domain; it contains target domain/workload and required outcome, never worker identity, runtime, strategy or priority.

Domain write authority is a separate CAS-headed authority surface. A production publication gate implements the existing DomainExecutionController publicationGate interface instead of introducing a second execution controller.

DomainExecutionController remains the generic post-claim HOW boundary. SA execution is selected later from SA-owned ExecutionPolicy and immutable ExecutionStrategyDescriptor; Integration C does not add an SA-specific scheduler or hard-coded execution strategy module.

Only a trusted accepted DomainPublicationReceipt may commit SemanticClaim revisions, CrossDomainObligation revisions and ProductDerivationEdge records into authoritative product truth; runtime proposedDerivationEdges remain proposals until publication.

SemanticClaim and CrossDomainObligation payloads are immutable. Separate CAS currentness heads point to the current revision and record ACTIVE, STALE, REVOKED or SUPERSEDED transitions without mutating historical evidence.

Logical obligation identity is normalized from project/root intent, issuing semantic subject, target domain/workload, obligation kind and stable obligation key. Replaying identical normalized content converges on one immutable revision; changed semantic content creates a new revision and supersedes the prior current head.

ProductDerivationEdge is a product-semantic dependency, not a Blackboard dependency. Reverse adjacency/impact indexes are rebuildable accelerators; immutable publication receipts, semantic revisions, edges and head transitions remain authority.

Selective invalidation starts from exact superseded semantic subject keys and follows reverse-transitive authoritative ProductDerivationEdge closure. Only impacted claim/obligation heads transition non-current; unrelated siblings remain current.

Dependent publication uses a two-observation currentness handshake: capture every consumed semantic-head revision before publication, persist the publication under the guarded write-authority/lifecycle window, then revalidate those exact observations before the dependent head can remain current. Drift forces deterministic stale reconciliation.

Cross-domain work materialization consumes an exact ACTIVE CrossDomainObligation revision plus its issuance/publication authority and existing materialization authorization. Stale/revoked/superseded obligations fail closed before new work can be created.

When an obligation becomes non-current, only Board work materialized from that exact obligation subject is affected. READY/REOPENED work is blocked; claimed/released work is invalidated through the existing organization claim lifecycle so executable capability is fenced before it can continue.
No LLM semantic-equivalence decision participates in invalidation pruning for v1. Precision comes from explicit stable semantic subject keys and accepted derivation edges.
implementationSlices: C1 — production domain write authority: implement DomainWriteAuthorityPolicy/current CAS head plus a trusted publication gate adapter for the existing DomainExecutionController; bind publisher principal/domain/allowed semantic and obligation kinds and preserve the current organization lifecycle publication fence.

C2 — immutable semantic subjects: implement content-addressed SemanticClaim and CrossDomainObligation revisions with separate CAS currentness heads, normalized logical keys, idempotent identical replay and explicit supersession/revocation transitions.

C3 — authoritative product lineage: persist ProductDerivationEdge only from accepted DomainPublicationReceipt publication, maintain rebuildable reverse-impact indexes, and implement deterministic reverse-transitive DependencyImpactAnalysis over exact semantic subject keys.

C4 — currentness reconciliation and work invalidation: perform the pre/post consumed-head handshake, mark raced dependents non-current, reject stale obligation materialization, and map an invalidated obligation only to work materialized from that exact obligation subject using existing block/invalidate/fence lifecycle seams.

C5 — BA -> SA executable vertical: publish an accepted BA requirement claim, issue one authorized SA solution-design obligation, materialize deterministic SA-owned work, prove BA never chooses SA worker/runtime/strategy, and show SA execution mechanics remain resolved by existing ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategyDescriptor infrastructure.

negativeVerificationCases: A BA publication that requests an obligation kind or target domain outside current DomainWriteAuthority is rejected before an obligation/head/work item is committed.
A CrossDomainObligation carrying worker identity, runtime, strategy or priority is rejected; the source domain cannot smuggle dispatch mechanics into WHAT.
Raw runtime proposedDerivationEdges without an accepted DomainPublicationReceipt never enter authoritative ProductDerivationEdge truth.
Replaying byte/semantic-equivalent normalized obligation publication does not create a second logical current revision or duplicate Board work.
Changing obligation semantics creates a new immutable revision and supersedes the prior head; the old historical revision remains resolvable.
Materialization from STALE, REVOKED or SUPERSEDED obligation currentness fails closed and creates no target work.
If an upstream subject changes while a dependent publication is in flight, the dependent cannot finish as silently current after the post-publication observation check.
Superseding one detail requirement invalidates only reverse-transitive detail/architecture dependents; an unrelated sibling/list claim remains ACTIVE and its work stays executable.
Blackboard task dependency edges alone never participate in product semantic invalidation.
Invalidation never resets the whole organization/stage and never reopens unrelated Board work.
Already-claimed work sourced from an invalidated obligation loses executable capability through canonical organization-claim invalidation/release fencing.
No model-produced semantic-equivalence guess may remove an edge or prune a required invalidation path.
